findings.where: The whole tile, and the first screen most of all: the hero holds only the section drawing, and no part of the tile shows a photograph of Mark or a slot for one
findings.fault: Mark is never seen. The tile shows no portrait and no stand-in labelled 'Placeholder', so it never shows how a photograph of a real person sits on a diazo-blue grid ground. The one picture is a drawing of a structure, so the page reads as a practice's drawing sheet, not as one named advisor.
findings.who_objects: A development bank officer checking who they would be hiring. A solo advisor's site has to show a real face before someone writes (first-visit trust item 1). Mark would object as well, since 'the man himself' is a client value every tile has to answer. Of all five grounds, blueprint paper is the hardest one to put a photograph on, and this tile leaves that problem unsolved for the layout round.

findings.where: Hero, the role line under the name ('INFRASTRUCTURE ADVISOR / LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A • SCALE NTS'), and the title block cells in the nav ('DRAWING MMM-GA-001', 'SCALE NTS'), which on the phone take the whole top row above the menu
findings.fault: Drawing-sheet jargon sits in the spots where a visitor looks for who Mark is and what he does, and it is given as much weight as his role. On a blueprint ground it suggests an engineering or design firm, but Mark is a lawyer and advisor. The direction card says the title block should carry the contact. Here it carries a drawing number and a scale that mean nothing to the visitor.
findings.who_objects: A procurement or PPP specialist at a development bank, in the first five seconds. They have to dig past 'Longitudinal section A-A' and 'NTS' to find that this is a legal advisor on PPP. The engineer's costume can give them the wrong idea of his profession before they reach the paragraph that corrects it.

findings.where: Hero, the amber 'WRITE TO MARK' button (a mailto: link), and the end of the tile, which has no footer or contact line
findings.fault: The email address never appears in full anywhere. The only contact route is a mailto: button, so a visitor whose machine has no mail client set up gets nothing when they click, and has no address to copy. The title block was supposed to carry the contact, but it doesn't.
findings.who_objects: A bank officer on a locked-down work laptop who uses webmail. When the button does nothing they cannot reach Mark, and an advisor whose address you can't see looks less reachable and less established (first-visit trust item 7: the address in full as its own link text).

findings.where: First screen: the heading, the summary and the amber button share the screen with the drawing from the first frame. The motion sketch says 'The linework is already on the sheet; only the cut and the light arrive'
findings.fault: Nothing waits. The name and the call to action ask for attention as soon as the picture appears. The direction card says the drawing fills the sheet first and the heading arrives after it. The tile's motion animates only the hatch and the light, and never holds back the words or the button.
findings.who_objects: Mark. 'Calm first: one quiet moment before any text asks for anything' is a client value, and it is the one principle v2 takes from Threlfall. Without that wait, this direction loses the quality it was chosen for.

findings.where: Article specimen, the byline 'MMM Infra Blog No. 8 • 18 September 2024'
findings.fault: The article is credited to the firm, not to Mark. No author name and no one-line bio appear on the deep page, so the first-person voice ('a client … asked me') belongs to nobody the reader can see.
findings.who_objects: A reader arriving from a LinkedIn post straight onto an article. They need the name and a line of standing to judge whether the opinion carries weight (first-visit trust item 12). Mark would also object: the individual is the brand and the voice is never a firm's (brand sheet §5).

findings.where: Hero summary, 'with over 40 years of international infrastructure experience'
findings.fault: The only claim about standing besides the World Bank role is a size word, and it gets the closing position in the hero's one strong line. It cannot be checked, and it reads as the kind of boast the brief rules out. The checkable fact next to it (Lead Lawyer, World Bank PPP Group) does the real work.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader who judges relevant experience by project kind and region, not by years. To them the years read as filler (Feel the CV: checkable specifics, never size words). Mark's own Infralegal take also asks for confidence without big-firm claims.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture row 'Streamlining the PPP Process … Lecture • 2026-04-23 · PDF', and the tile as a whole
findings.fault: The proof slot gives no venue or host body for the talk. Nowhere does the tile show third-party proof, or a link out to work that a named body hosts. The newest talk, the one item that could show standing through who asked, is reduced to a bare date.
findings.who_objects: A development bank officer looking for evidence that bodies like theirs have asked Mark to speak or advise. 'Lecture' with no host tells them nothing, and it gives the identity no pattern for showing proof (first-visit trust item 14; Feel the CV: the newest talk with its venue).
